The debtor must have rights in the collateral
questions.exp: Attachment under UCC 9-203 requires value, the debtor's rights in the collateral, and an authenticated security agreement (or possession or control). Filing relates to perfection, not attachment.

questions.q: On March 1, Year 1, Lender properly filed a financing statement covering Borrower's equipment. No continuation statement has been filed. Which statement is correct?
choices: A continuation statement may be filed at any time after the original filing
The financing statement lapses after three years
The financing statement lapses on March 1, Year 6, unless a continuation statement is filed within the six months before that date
The financing statement remains effective until the loan is repaid
questions.exp: A financing statement is generally effective for five years (UCC 9-515) and may be continued only by a continuation statement filed within six months before lapse. A continuation filed earlier is ineffective, and lapse makes the interest unperfected.

questions.q: An appliance store sold a refrigerator on credit to Fran for use in her home and took a written security agreement covering the refrigerator. The store did not file a financing statement. Is the store's security interest perfected?
choices: Yes, because a purchase-money security interest in consumer goods is perfected automatically on attachment
Yes, but only for 20 days after the sale
No, because the store did not take possession of the refrigerator
No, because a financing statement must be filed for all goods
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-309, a PMSI in consumer goods (other than titled goods such as motor vehicles) is automatically perfected when it attaches. The 20-day period relates to PMSI priority in other collateral, not automatic perfection.

questions.q: A store holds an automatically perfected purchase-money security interest, with no financing statement filed, in a television it sold on credit to Gina for household use. Gina sold the television at a garage sale to her neighbor, Hal, who paid cash, did not know of the security interest, and bought it for his own household use. Does Hal take the television subject to the store's security interest?
choices: No, because Hal bought for value, without knowledge, for personal use, before any financing statement was filed
Yes, because the store's interest was perfected
No, because a security interest never follows goods sold by a consumer
Yes, because Hal is not a buyer in the ordinary course of business
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-320, a consumer buyer from a consumer takes free of an automatically perfected PMSI if he buys without knowledge, for value, for personal or household use and before a financing statement is filed. Filing would have protected the store.

questions.q: First Bank has a perfected security interest in all of Dealer's inventory of new cars, and its financing statement is on file. Kay bought a car from Dealer's lot for her personal use, paying full price. Kay knew that Dealer financed its inventory through First Bank. Dealer then defaulted. Does Kay take the car free of First Bank's security interest?
choices: No, because Kay knew of the financing arrangement
Yes, but only if Kay paid in cash
Yes, because Kay is a buyer in the ordinary course of business
No, because First Bank's security interest was perfected by filing
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-320, a buyer in the ordinary course of business takes free of a security interest created by the seller, even if perfected and even if the buyer knows of it. Only knowledge that the sale violates the security agreement defeats ordinary-course status.

questions.q: On January 5, Alpha Bank filed a financing statement covering Max's equipment. On January 10, Beta Bank lent Max money, took a security agreement covering the same equipment and filed a financing statement. On February 1, Alpha Bank lent Max money and Max signed a security agreement. Neither interest is a purchase-money security interest. Which bank has priority?
choices: Beta Bank, because it was perfected first
Beta Bank, because its security interest attached first
The banks share pro rata
Alpha Bank, because it filed first
questions.exp: Between perfected security interests, priority goes to the first to file or perfect (UCC 9-322), and a financing statement may be filed before attachment. Alpha filed on January 5, before Beta did anything.

questions.q: Cora Bank and Dale Finance each obtained a security interest in the same equipment of a debtor. Cora's attached on May 1 and was never perfected. Dale's attached on June 1 and was perfected by filing on June 2. Which creditor has priority?
choices: Neither, because the interests are equal
Cora Bank, unless Dale knew of Cora's interest
Cora Bank, because its interest attached first
Dale Finance, because a perfected security interest has priority over an unperfected one
questions.exp: A perfected security interest has priority over a conflicting unperfected one (UCC 9-322); attachment order matters only between two unperfected interests. Article 9 has no knowledge exception for this rule.

questions.q: Old Bank has a perfected security interest, with an after-acquired property clause, in all of Retailer's present and future inventory. New Supplier sells additional inventory to Retailer on credit and wants priority over Old Bank in that inventory. What must New Supplier do?
choices: Nothing, because purchase-money interests always have priority
Perfect its purchase-money security interest by the time Retailer receives the inventory and send authenticated notice to Old Bank before then
File a financing statement within 20 days after Retailer receives the inventory
Obtain Old Bank's written consent
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-324, a PMSI in inventory has priority over an earlier-filed interest only if it is perfected when the debtor receives the inventory and the purchase-money creditor sends authenticated notification to the prior secured party beforehand. The 20-day grace period applies to non-inventory collateral such as equipment.

questions.q: Eagle Bank has a perfected security interest in all of Ford Co.'s present and after-acquired equipment. Ford bought a new machine from a vendor on credit, giving the vendor a purchase-money security interest. Ford received the machine on April 1, and the vendor filed a financing statement on April 15. Which party has priority in the machine?
choices: Eagle Bank, because the vendor did not notify it before delivery
The vendor, but only if Eagle Bank knew of the sale
Eagle Bank, because it filed first
The vendor, because it perfected its purchase-money security interest within 20 days after Ford received possession
questions.exp: A PMSI in goods other than inventory has priority over a conflicting earlier interest if perfected when the debtor receives possession or within 20 days thereafter (UCC 9-324). No notice to the earlier secured party is required for equipment.

questions.q: Glen lent money to Hart Co. and obtained a signed security agreement covering Hart's equipment, but never filed a financing statement. Later, a judgment creditor of Hart levied on the equipment, becoming a lien creditor. Hart then filed for bankruptcy. Which statement is correct?
choices: Glen has priority because his security interest attached first
Glen has priority because the lien creditor had notice
Glen and the lien creditor share pro rata
The lien creditor, and the bankruptcy trustee, have priority over Glen's unperfected security interest
questions.exp: An unperfected security interest is subordinate to a person who becomes a lien creditor before perfection (UCC 9-317), and the bankruptcy trustee has the status of a hypothetical lien creditor. Perfection is essential to protect against third parties.

questions.q: Bank lends money to Ivy Corp. and takes a security interest in Ivy's deposit account at another bank as original collateral (not as proceeds). How may Bank perfect its security interest?
choices: By filing a financing statement
By taking possession of Ivy's checkbook
Automatically upon attachment
Only by obtaining control of the deposit account
questions.exp: A security interest in a deposit account as original collateral may be perfected only by control (UCC 9-312, 9-314), for example through an agreement with the depositary bank. Filing is ineffective for deposit accounts.

questions.q: Jade Bank has a security interest in Kent's equipment, perfected by filing. Kent sold a piece of the equipment without authorization and deposited the cash proceeds in a separate account where they remain identifiable. Which statement is correct?
choices: Jade's security interest ended when the equipment was sold
Jade's security interest continues in the identifiable cash proceeds and remains perfected
Jade must file a new financing statement within 10 days to reach the proceeds
Jade's security interest attaches to the proceeds but is unperfected
questions.exp: A security interest continues in collateral after an unauthorized disposition and attaches to identifiable proceeds (UCC 9-315); if the original interest was perfected by filing, perfection continues in identifiable cash proceeds beyond the 20-day period. No new filing is needed for identifiable cash proceeds.

questions.q: A security agreement grants Lender an interest in 'all of Debtor's equipment, now owned or hereafter acquired.' Debtor, a manufacturer, later buys a new forklift for its plant. Which statement is correct?
choices: The clause covers the forklift only if acquired within 10 days of the agreement
After-acquired property clauses are unenforceable under Article 9
Lender must obtain a new security agreement to cover the forklift
Lender's security interest attaches to the forklift when Debtor acquires rights in it
questions.exp: After-acquired property clauses are valid (UCC 9-204) and the interest attaches when the debtor acquires rights in new collateral. The 10-day limit applies only to consumer goods given as additional security.

questions.q: A piano teacher bought a grand piano that she uses exclusively in her studio to give paid lessons. How is the piano classified as collateral under Article 9?
choices: Consumer goods
Inventory
Equipment
General intangibles
questions.exp: Goods are classified by the debtor's primary use; goods used primarily in a business that are not inventory or farm products are equipment (UCC 9-102). The same piano would be consumer goods if bought for household use, or inventory if held for sale.

questions.q: Nova Corp. is incorporated in Delaware, has its headquarters in Ohio, and keeps the equipment that will serve as collateral in Texas. Where should a lender file a financing statement to perfect a security interest in Nova's equipment?
choices: Texas, where the equipment is located
Delaware, Nova's state of organization
In all three states
Ohio, where Nova's chief executive office is located
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-301 and 9-307, perfection by filing is governed by the law of the debtor's location, and a registered organization such as a corporation is located in its state of organization. Location of the collateral or headquarters is irrelevant for this purpose.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT required for a financing statement to be sufficient under Article 9?
choices: The name of the secured party or its representative
An indication of the collateral covered
The debtor's signature
The name of the debtor
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-502, a financing statement needs only the debtor's name, the secured party's name and an indication of collateral; the debtor need only authorize the filing, not sign it. An authenticated security agreement is required for attachment, not the financing statement.

questions.q: Debtor defaulted on a loan secured by a truck. In the middle of the night, the secured party towed the truck from Debtor's open driveway without confrontation and without a court order. Was the repossession proper?
choices: No, because Debtor did not consent at the time
Yes, but only if Debtor was given 10 days' advance notice
Yes, because a secured party may repossess without judicial process if it does so without a breach of the peace
No, because repossession always requires a court order
questions.exp: UCC 9-609 permits self-help repossession after default if it proceeds without a breach of the peace; taking a vehicle from an open driveway without confrontation is generally permissible. No prior notice or court order is required.

questions.q: A store holds a purchase-money security interest in a consumer's home entertainment system. The consumer paid 70% of the cash price and then defaulted. The store repossessed the system. Absent a post-default waiver by the consumer, what must the store do?
choices: The store may keep the system and also sue for the unpaid balance
The store may keep the system in full satisfaction of the debt
The store must dispose of the system within 90 days after taking possession
The store must return the system to the consumer
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-620, when a consumer has paid 60% or more of the cash price of PMSI consumer goods, the secured party must dispose of the collateral within 90 days rather than retain it in satisfaction, unless the consumer waives this after default. Strict foreclosure is otherwise allowed only with consent.

questions.q: After default, a secured party sold the collateral for $12,000. The secured debt was $10,000, and reasonable repossession and sale expenses were $1,000. A subordinate secured party with a $500 claim sent an authenticated demand for proceeds before distribution. How much is the debtor entitled to receive?
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-615, proceeds go first to expenses ($1,000), then to the secured debt ($10,000), then to subordinate secured parties that made a demand ($500), and the remaining $500 surplus goes to the debtor. Ignoring the subordinate creditor gives $1,000.

questions.q: A debtor owed $20,000 on a loan secured by equipment. After default, the secured party repossessed and sold the equipment in a commercially reasonable manner for $14,000, incurring $1,500 of reasonable expenses. The transaction is not a consumer transaction. What is the debtor's liability?
choices: $0, because repossession satisfies the debt
questions.exp: Proceeds are applied first to expenses, leaving $12,500 for the $20,000 debt, so the debtor owes a $7,500 deficiency (UCC 9-615). Ignoring the expenses gives $6,000.

questions.q: A secured party repossessed a debtor's equipment after default and scheduled a public sale. Before the sale, the debtor offered to pay the missed installments only. Which statement is correct?
choices: The debtor may redeem the collateral only by tendering the full obligation secured plus reasonable expenses before disposition
The debtor has no right to redeem once the collateral is repossessed
The debtor may redeem within one year after the sale
The debtor may redeem by paying only the missed installments
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-623, the debtor may redeem before the secured party disposes of or accepts the collateral by fulfilling all obligations secured, plus reasonable expenses (accelerated balance if acceleration applies). Redemption rights end at disposition.

questions.q: A secured party plans to sell repossessed manufacturing equipment at a private sale. Which statement about notice is correct?
choices: No notice is required for a private sale
Notice is required only if the collateral is consumer goods
The secured party generally must send reasonable authenticated notification of the disposition to the debtor and any secondary obligors
Notice must be published in a newspaper for 30 days
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-611, a secured party must send reasonable authenticated notice of disposition to the debtor, secondary obligors and certain other secured parties, except for perishable collateral or goods sold on a recognized market. Every aspect of the disposition must be commercially reasonable.

questions.q: Which transaction creates a purchase-money security interest?
choices: A bank refinances an existing unsecured loan and takes a security interest in the borrower's inventory
A bank lends money that the borrower uses to buy a delivery van and takes a security interest in the van
A bank lends money for working capital and takes a security interest in the borrower's existing equipment
A supplier takes a security interest in a customer's accounts receivable to secure past-due invoices
questions.exp: A PMSI arises when the secured party (a seller or lender) gives value that enables the debtor to acquire the collateral (UCC 9-103). Security interests in property the debtor already owns, or securing antecedent debts, are not purchase-money.

questions.q: Opie borrowed $1,000 from Pam and orally agreed that Pam could hold Opie's diamond ring as collateral. Pam took the ring. No written agreement was signed. Which statement is correct?
choices: Pam has an unperfected security interest until she files a financing statement
Pam must file to perfect because jewelry is consumer goods
Pam has an attached and perfected security interest by possession
Pam has no security interest because there was no written security agreement
questions.exp: When the secured party takes possession under the debtor's security agreement, an oral agreement satisfies attachment (UCC 9-203), and possession perfects the interest in goods (UCC 9-313). An authenticated writing is required only when the secured party does not have possession or control.

questions.q: Mortgage Bank recorded a mortgage on Rob's commercial building. Later, Rob bought an industrial furnace on credit from Seller, which retained a purchase-money security interest. The furnace became a fixture on June 1, and Seller made a proper fixture filing on June 10. Who has priority in the furnace?
choices: Mortgage Bank, because fixtures become part of the real estate
Seller, but only if Mortgage Bank consented in writing
Mortgage Bank, because its mortgage was recorded first
Seller, because it made a fixture filing for its PMSI within 20 days after the goods became fixtures
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-334, a PMSI in fixtures has priority over an earlier real estate interest if the interest is perfected by a fixture filing before the goods become fixtures or within 20 days thereafter. The general first-in-time rule yields to this purchase-money exception.

questions.q: A secured party holds a debtor's valuable painting as pledged collateral. Which duty does the secured party owe while in possession?
choices: A duty to use reasonable care in the custody and preservation of the collateral
A duty to insure the painting for its full value at its own expense
No duty, because the debtor bears all risk of loss
A duty to return the painting on demand before the debt is paid
questions.exp: UCC 9-207 requires a secured party in possession to use reasonable care in custody and preservation; reasonable expenses, including insurance, are chargeable to the debtor and secured by the collateral. Return is required only when the obligation is satisfied.

questions.q: Sue, an individual, borrowed money from Credit Union to buy a car for personal use, granting a security interest in the car. The state has a certificate-of-title statute covering motor vehicles. How does Credit Union perfect its security interest?
choices: By having its security interest noted on the car's certificate of title
By filing a financing statement with the secretary of state
By taking possession of the car keys
Automatically, because it is a purchase-money security interest in consumer goods
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-311, security interests in goods covered by a certificate-of-title statute are perfected by compliance with that statute, usually notation on the title. Automatic PMSI perfection for consumer goods does not extend to titled motor vehicles.

questions.q: Tom paid off in full a loan secured by his household furniture. A financing statement had been filed. What is the secured party's obligation regarding the filing?
choices: To file a termination statement only if Tom pays a fee
None; the financing statement simply lapses after five years
To return the original financing statement to Tom
To file a termination statement within one month after the obligation is satisfied, or within 20 days after an authenticated demand if earlier
questions.exp: For financing statements covering consumer goods, UCC 9-513 requires the secured party to file a termination statement within one month after the obligation ends, or within 20 days after an authenticated demand, whichever is earlier. For non-consumer collateral, it must act on demand.

questions.q: Uma, an individual, granted Bank a security interest in her equipment, which Bank perfected by filing in State X, where Uma lived. Uma then moved her principal residence to State Y. Bank did nothing. Which statement is correct?
choices: Bank's perfection continues for the remainder of the five-year filing period
Bank must refile in State Y within 20 days
Bank's perfection continues for four months after the move, and Bank must perfect in State Y within that period to remain continuously perfected
Bank's perfection lapses immediately upon the move
questions.exp: Under UCC 9-316, when the debtor's location changes to another jurisdiction, perfection continues for four months (or until the filing would have lapsed, if sooner); if the secured party does not perfect in the new state within that time, the interest is deemed never perfected against purchasers for value.

questions.q: Factor Co. bought Vale Co.'s accounts receivable outright for cash. Which statement is correct?
choices: Article 9 does not apply because the transaction is a sale, not a loan
Article 9 applies to the sale of accounts, so Factor Co. must generally file a financing statement to perfect its interest
Account debtors must pay Factor Co. even before they are notified of the sale
Factor Co.'s interest is automatically perfected regardless of the size of the transaction
questions.exp: Article 9 applies to sales of accounts and payment intangibles as well as secured loans (UCC 9-109), and the buyer generally perfects by filing; automatic perfection applies only to insignificant assignments. Account debtors may pay the assignor until notified (UCC 9-406).

questions.q: A tax-exempt private university engages in several income-producing activities. Which activity most likely generates unrelated business taxable income?
choices: Receiving royalties for licensing the university's name on apparel
Selling donated clothing at a thrift shop
Operating a commercial dry-cleaning business open to the general public year-round
Receiving dividends on its endowment's publicly traded stock (not debt-financed)
questions.exp: UBTI arises from a trade or business regularly carried on that is not substantially related to the exempt purpose (§§511-513); a commercial dry cleaner serving the public qualifies. Dividends and royalties are excluded passive income, and sales of donated goods fall within a statutory exception.

questions.q: A charitable hospital operates a gift shop that sells purchased (not donated) merchandise to the general public. The shop is open daily and is staffed entirely by unpaid volunteers. How is the gift shop's net income treated?
choices: It is excluded from unrelated business taxable income because substantially all the work is performed by volunteers
It causes the hospital to lose its exemption
It is unrelated business taxable income because the merchandise was purchased
It is taxable because the shop is regularly carried on
questions.exp: Section 513 excludes any trade or business in which substantially all the work is performed without compensation. The source of the merchandise matters only for the donated-goods exception, which is a separate exclusion.

questions.q: A tax-exempt organization borrowed money to purchase publicly traded stock as an investment. The acquisition indebtedness is outstanding throughout the year. How are the dividends on the stock treated?
choices: Included in UBTI only if the stock is sold during the year
Entirely excluded from UBTI, because dividends are passive investment income
Entirely included in UBTI
Included in UBTI in proportion to the average acquisition indebtedness relative to the property's average adjusted basis
questions.exp: Under §514, income from debt-financed property is included in UBTI in the ratio of average acquisition indebtedness to average adjusted basis, overriding the normal dividend exclusion. The passive-income exclusion does not protect debt-financed property.

questions.q: A calendar-year exempt organization had $1,500 of gross income from an unrelated trade or business and $700 of directly connected expenses. Which statement is correct?
choices: It must file Form 990-T only if it is a private foundation
It must file Form 990-T because its gross unrelated business income is $1,000 or more
It must report the income on Form 990 but not Form 990-T
It owes no return because its net unrelated income is less than $1,000
questions.exp: Form 990-T is required when gross UBI is $1,000 or more (Reg. §1.6012-2), even though the $1,000 specific deduction under §512 will eliminate the tax here. Testing the filing threshold against net income is the trap.

questions.q: Which of the following tax-exempt organizations is NOT required to file an annual information return (Form 990 series)?
choices: A church
A private foundation
A trade association with $2 million of annual gross receipts
A charitable hospital with $2 million of annual gross receipts
questions.exp: Churches, their integrated auxiliaries and conventions of churches are excepted from filing under §6033. Private foundations must always file Form 990-PF regardless of size.

questions.q: Which organization most likely is a private foundation rather than a public charity?
choices: A hospital providing medical care to the public
A church that receives contributions from hundreds of members
A charitable organization funded by a single family's contributions and supported mainly by its investment income
A college with a regular faculty and enrolled student body
questions.exp: Under §509, a §501 charitable organization is a private foundation unless it is a listed public institution (church, school, hospital) or meets a public support test. A single-family-funded investment-supported entity fails the public support tests.

questions.q: A private nonoperating foundation's noncharitable-use assets had an average fair market value of $10,000,000 for the year. Ignoring the excise tax on net investment income, what is the foundation's approximate minimum required distribution?
choices: $0, because private foundations have no distribution requirement
questions.exp: Section 4942 requires a private nonoperating foundation to distribute a minimum investment return of 5% of its noncharitable-use assets: 5% × $10,000,000 = $500,000. Failure triggers an excise tax on the undistributed amount.

questions.q: A substantial contributor to a private foundation sold land to the foundation at its appraised fair market value. Which statement is correct?
choices: The sale is permitted because it was at fair market value
The sale is an act of self-dealing subject to excise tax, even at fair market value
The sale is self-dealing only if the price exceeded fair market value
The sale is permitted if the board approves it
questions.exp: Section 4941 treats any sale or exchange of property between a private foundation and a disqualified person as self-dealing, regardless of fairness. The arm's-length defense that applies elsewhere does not apply here.

questions.q: A newly formed charitable organization (not a church) expects annual gross receipts well over $5,000. To be recognized as a §501 charitable organization from its date of formation, what must it generally do?
choices: File an application for recognition of exemption within 27 months after the end of the month in which it was organized
File an application within 15 months after formation; no extension is available
Do nothing, because charitable organizations are automatically exempt
File its first Form 990 within 12 months of formation
questions.exp: Under §508 and the regulations, a charitable organization must notify the IRS (Form 1023) to be treated as exempt, and recognition is retroactive to formation if filed within 27 months (15 months plus the automatic 12-month extension). Churches and small organizations are excepted.

questions.q: Which activity would jeopardize the tax-exempt status of a §501 charitable public charity?
choices: Holding a forum at which all qualified candidates are invited to speak
Publicly endorsing a candidate for elective public office
Spending an insubstantial amount of its budget on lobbying for legislation
Conducting nonpartisan voter registration drives
questions.exp: Charitable organizations are absolutely prohibited from participating in political campaigns for or against any candidate. Insubstantial lobbying and nonpartisan voter education are permitted.

questions.q: A corporation's only activity is operating a for-profit chain of retail stores, and it pays all of its profits to a charitable hospital. Is the corporation exempt from income tax?
choices: No, because an organization operated primarily to carry on a trade or business for profit is not exempt merely because its profits go to an exempt organization
Yes, if the hospital owns all of its stock
Yes, because all of its profits go to an exempt organization
No, unless the profits exceed $1 million
questions.exp: Under the feeder organization rule of §502, an entity whose primary purpose is a business for profit is not exempt on the ground that all its profits are payable to an exempt organization. The destination of profits does not make an activity exempt.

questions.q: A charitable organization received payments from local businesses in connection with its annual fundraising run. Which payment is most likely unrelated business income?
choices: A payment acknowledged by listing the business's name in the program as a sponsor
A payment for an advertisement in the program that includes the business's prices and an endorsement
A payment acknowledged by displaying the business's name and logo on the event banner
A payment acknowledged by mentioning the business's location and phone number
questions.exp: Under §513, qualified sponsorship payments that receive only an acknowledgment (name, logo, location) are excluded, but advertising containing qualitative or comparative language, price information or endorsements is a substantial return benefit and can generate UBI.

questions.q: Contributions to which of the following organizations are deductible as charitable contributions by an individual donor?
choices: A social welfare organization that engages in substantial lobbying
A public charity organized and operated exclusively for educational purposes
A members-only country club (social club)
A local chamber of commerce (business league)
questions.exp: Section 170 charitable deductions are generally limited to organizations organized and operated exclusively for charitable, educational, religious and similar purposes. Social welfare organizations, business leagues and social clubs may be exempt but do not qualify to receive deductible contributions.

questions.q: An exempt social club (country club) earned dividends and interest from investing its members' dues. How is this investment income treated?
choices: It is excluded from UBTI, as it would be for a charitable organization
It causes the club to lose its exemption
It is taxed only if the investments are debt-financed
It is generally included in UBTI, because social clubs are taxed on income other than exempt function income
questions.exp: Section 512 provides a special rule for social clubs: UBTI includes all gross income other than exempt function income (member dues and fees), so investment income is taxable. The passive-income exclusion that protects charities does not apply.

questions.q: An exempt organization leases a building together with furniture and equipment to an unrelated tenant. Thirty percent of the total rent is attributable to the personal property. Rent is a fixed amount not based on the tenant's income, and there is no debt on the property. How is the rent treated?
choices: Only the rent attributable to the personal property is included in UBTI
Only the rent attributable to the real property is included in UBTI
All of the rent is included in UBTI
All of the rent is excluded from UBTI
questions.exp: Under §512, rents from real property are excluded, and incidental personal property rent (10% or less) is also excluded; if personal property rent is more than 10% but not more than 50%, only the personal property portion is UBTI. All rent becomes UBTI only above 50%.

questions.q: An exempt organization had $50,000 of gross income from an unrelated trade or business and $20,000 of directly connected expenses. Assuming no other unrelated activities, what is its unrelated business taxable income?
questions.exp: UBTI equals gross UBI less directly connected deductions less the $1,000 specific deduction of §512: $50,000 − $20,000 − $1,000 = $29,000. Forgetting the specific deduction gives $30,000.

questions.q: Which of the following sources of income of a charitable organization is excluded from unrelated business taxable income by a specific statutory exception?
choices: Income from a commercial parking lot open to the public
Income from a restaurant open to the public in a downtown office building
Income from bingo games that are legal under state and local law
Income from regularly selling advertising in its monthly journal
questions.exp: Section 513 specifically excludes qualified bingo game income where the games are legal under state and local law. Advertising, public parking lots and restaurants are regularly carried on commercial activities that generally produce UBTI.

questions.q: Which provision in an organization's articles of incorporation is required to satisfy the organizational test for a §501 charitable organization?
choices: A provision limiting its purposes to exempt purposes and dedicating its assets to exempt purposes upon dissolution
A provision requiring that a majority of its board be public officials
A provision allowing distribution of net earnings to members upon dissolution
A provision permitting the organization to engage in political campaigns
questions.exp: Under Reg. §1.501-1, the articles must limit purposes to exempt purposes, not empower substantial non-exempt activities, and dedicate assets to exempt purposes on dissolution. Distributing assets to members would violate the prohibition on private inurement.

questions.q: A public charity paid its executive director, a disqualified person, compensation substantially in excess of reasonable compensation for the services provided. What is the most likely federal tax consequence?
choices: An excise tax imposed on the executive director on the excess benefit, with a possible tax on managers who knowingly approved it
An excise tax imposed on the charity equal to the entire compensation
Automatic revocation of the charity's exemption
No consequence, because public charities may set compensation freely
questions.exp: The intermediate sanctions of §4958 impose an excise tax on the disqualified person who receives an excess benefit (and on knowing managers), as an alternative to revocation. The tax is measured by the excess, not the entire payment.

questions.q: Which of the following is a taxable expenditure of a private foundation?
choices: A grant to a public charity for its general operations
A travel grant to an individual awarded without IRS-approved procedures
Scholarships awarded on an objective, nondiscriminatory basis under procedures approved in advance by the IRS
Reasonable compensation paid to a foundation manager for necessary services
questions.exp: Under §4945, grants to individuals for travel, study or similar purposes are taxable expenditures unless made under procedures approved in advance by the IRS. Grants to public charities and reasonable compensation are not taxable expenditures.

questions.q: Which statement about public disclosure by a tax-exempt charitable public charity is correct?
choices: It must make its exemption application and its annual information returns for the three most recent years available for public inspection, but generally need not disclose the names of its contributors
It must disclose only its exemption application, not its annual returns
It need not make any returns available to the public
It must disclose the names and addresses of all contributors on request
questions.exp: Section 6104 requires exempt organizations to make their exemption application and their three most recent annual returns available, but public charities may withhold contributor names and addresses. Private foundations, by contrast, must disclose their contributors.

questions.q: When is the annual information return (Form 990) of a calendar-year exempt organization organized as a corporation due, before extensions?
choices: March 15
June 15
May 15
April 15
questions.exp: Form 990 is due on the 15th day of the fifth month after the end of the organization's tax year (§6072), which is May 15 for a calendar-year organization. April 15 is the due date for individual and C corporation income tax returns.

questions.q: A charity held a fundraising dinner. Each donor paid $100 and received a meal worth $40. What must the charity do?
choices: Report the full $100 as unrelated business income
Withhold income tax on the $40 meal value
Provide a written statement informing donors that only $60 is deductible and stating the value of the meal
Nothing, because the payment is under $250
questions.exp: Under §6115, a charity receiving a quid pro quo contribution exceeding $75 must provide a written statement that the deduction is limited to the excess of the payment over the value of goods or services ($60) and a good-faith estimate of their value. The $250 threshold applies to the donor's substantiation rule, not quid pro quo disclosure.

questions.q: An exempt organization that is required to file an annual information return failed to file for three consecutive years. What is the consequence?
choices: Its tax-exempt status is automatically revoked
A late filing penalty only; its exemption is unaffected
It is reclassified as a private foundation
Its exemption is revoked only after an IRS audit
questions.exp: Section 6033 provides for automatic revocation of exemption when an organization fails to file a required return or notice for three consecutive years. The organization must reapply to regain exemption.

questions.q: Which type of tax-exempt organization may engage in unlimited lobbying related to its exempt purpose without jeopardizing its exemption?
choices: A charitable public charity
A church
A private foundation
A social welfare organization
questions.exp: Social welfare organizations may lobby without limit if the lobbying furthers their social welfare purpose, although contributions to them are not deductible. Charitable organizations, including churches, may conduct only insubstantial lobbying, and private foundation lobbying is a taxable expenditure.

questions.q: An individual with adjusted gross income of $100,000 contributed $40,000 of cash to a private nonoperating foundation. He made no other contributions. How much may he deduct this year?
questions.exp: Cash contributions to private nonoperating foundations are limited to 30% of AGI under §170, or $30,000, with the $10,000 excess carried forward five years. The higher limit applies to public charities, and the 20% limit applies to capital gain property given to private foundations.

questions.q: Which of the following is included in the unrelated business taxable income of a charitable hospital?
choices: Interest on corporate bonds that are not debt-financed
Royalties from licensing a patent
Gain on the sale of investment securities that are not debt-financed
Net income from regularly selling pharmaceuticals to the general public who are not hospital patients
questions.exp: Regular sales of pharmaceuticals to the general public are not substantially related to the hospital's exempt function of caring for patients, so they produce UBTI. Royalties, interest and capital gains are excluded by the §512 modifications.

questions.q: An exempt organization owns 80% of a taxable subsidiary and receives rent from it. The subsidiary deducts the rent in computing its taxable income. How is the rent treated by the exempt parent?
choices: Included in UBTI only if the property is personal property
Excluded from UBTI if the rent is at fair market value
Included in UBTI to the extent the payment reduces the subsidiary's net income
Excluded from UBTI, because rents from real property are always excluded
questions.exp: Under §512, interest, annuities, royalties and rents received from a controlled entity (more than 50%) are included in UBTI to the extent they reduce the controlled entity's net income. This prevents shifting taxable income to the exempt parent.

questions.q: At what rates is the unrelated business taxable income of an exempt organization organized as a corporation taxed?
choices: It is not taxed if the income is used for exempt purposes
At a flat excise tax rate on investment income
At the compressed rates applicable to trusts
At the regular corporate income tax rate
questions.exp: Under §511, UBTI of an exempt corporation is taxed at corporate rates, while an exempt trust's UBTI is taxed at trust rates. Use of the income for exempt purposes does not eliminate the tax.

questions.q: An exempt organization operates two separate unrelated trades or businesses: a parking garage with $30,000 of net income and a catering business with a $12,000 net loss. What is the organization's UBTI before the specific deduction?
questions.exp: Under §512, UBTI is computed separately for each unrelated trade or business, and a loss from one cannot offset income from another; the catering loss is carried forward against that activity's future income. Netting the two gives $18,000, which the 'silo' rule prohibits.

questions.q: A simple trust earned $30,000 of dividends and $10,000 of taxable interest during the year, and realized an $8,000 long-term capital gain that the trust instrument allocates to corpus. The trust had no expenses and distributed all of its accounting income to the beneficiary. What is the trust's taxable income?
questions.exp: The $40,000 distribution deduction removes all ordinary income; the corpus capital gain is taxed to the trust, less the $300 exemption for a trust required to distribute all income (§642): $8,000 − $300 = $7,700. Forgetting the exemption gives $8,000.

questions.q: A trust's governing instrument permits the trustee to accumulate income. This year, the trustee nevertheless distributed all of the trust's accounting income and none of its corpus. What personal exemption may the trust deduct?
questions.exp: Under §642, the $300 exemption is available only to a trust required by its instrument to distribute all income currently; other trusts get $100, even if they happen to distribute all income. The $600 exemption is for estates.

questions.q: A complex trust had $20,000 of taxable interest, $10,000 of tax-exempt interest, a $3,000 trustee fee charged to income, and a $15,000 capital gain allocated to corpus. It distributed $27,000 to its sole beneficiary. The fee is not directly attributable to either type of interest. What is the trust's distribution deduction?
questions.exp: DNI is $27,000 ($30,000 − $3,000 fee, excluding the corpus gain); one-third of the fee ($1,000) is allocated to exempt income, leaving $9,000 of tax-exempt DNI, which is excluded from the deduction under §661, so the deduction is $18,000. Allocating the entire fee to taxable income gives $17,000.

questions.q: Under what circumstances are capital gains of a trust included in distributable net income (DNI)?
choices: When they are allocated to income under the governing instrument or local law, or are paid, credited or required to be distributed, as in a trust's final year
Only for simple trusts
Always, because DNI is based on taxable income
Never, because capital gains are always taxed to the trust
questions.exp: Under §643 and Reg. §1.643-3, capital gains allocated to corpus and not distributed are excluded from DNI, but gains allocated to income or actually distributed (including in the termination year) are included. The general rule excluding them is not absolute.

questions.q: A complex trust has DNI and accounting income of $40,000, all taxable interest. The instrument requires $30,000 to be distributed annually to Ann. The trustee also made a discretionary distribution of $30,000 to Bob. How much income must Bob report from the trust?
questions.exp: Under the tier system of §662, first-tier (required) distributions absorb DNI first: Ann reports $30,000, leaving $10,000 of DNI for Bob's second-tier distribution. Allocating DNI pro rata to both beneficiaries gives $20,000, which ignores the tiers.

questions.q: A complex trust uses the calendar year. On February 20 of the following year, the trustee made a discretionary distribution to a beneficiary. Which statement is correct?
choices: The distribution must be reported in the year paid; no election is available
The trustee may elect to treat the distribution as made on the last day of the prior year because it was made within 65 days after year-end
Only estates may elect to treat late distributions as made in the prior year
The distribution automatically relates back to the prior year
questions.exp: The 65-day rule of §663 lets the fiduciary of a complex trust (or estate) elect to treat distributions within the first 65 days of the year as made in the prior year. It is elective, not automatic.

questions.q: Lynn created a trust and retained the power to revoke it at any time. During the year the trust earned $50,000 of taxable interest, all of which the trustee distributed to Lynn's adult daughter. Who is taxed on the $50,000?
choices: The daughter, because she received the distribution
The daughter and the trust equally
The trust, because it is a separate taxable entity
Lynn, because the trust is a grantor trust
questions.exp: A grantor who retains the power to revoke is treated as owner of the trust under §676 and is taxed on all its income, regardless of who receives distributions. The normal DNI conduit rules do not apply to grantor trusts.

questions.q: Which of the following causes the grantor to be treated as the owner of a trust for income tax purposes?
choices: An independent trustee may accumulate income for the grantor's grandchildren
The grantor retains a reversionary interest worth 3% of the trust's value at inception
The grantor retains a reversionary interest worth more than 5% of the trust's value at inception
An independent bank trustee may distribute income among the grantor's adult children
questions.exp: Under §673, a reversionary interest exceeding 5% of the trust's value at inception makes the grantor the owner. Powers held by independent trustees to sprinkle income are excepted under §674.

questions.q: Which statement about the taxable year of estates and trusts is correct?
choices: Both estates and trusts must use a calendar year
An estate may adopt a fiscal year, but a trust (other than certain tax-exempt and charitable trusts) must use a calendar year
A trust may adopt a fiscal year, but an estate must use a calendar year
Both estates and trusts may adopt any fiscal year
questions.exp: Section 644 requires trusts to use the calendar year, while an estate may choose a fiscal year ending at the end of any month within its first 12 months. The fiscal-year option for estates is a planning tool for deferral.

questions.q: Which statement about estimated tax payments by estates and trusts is correct?
choices: An estate is not required to make estimated payments for tax years ending within two years after the decedent's death
Estates and trusts are never required to make estimated payments
Estates must make estimated payments beginning with their first tax year
A trust is exempt from estimated payments for its first two tax years
questions.exp: Under §6654, estates (and grantor trusts receiving the residue under a will) are exempt from estimated tax for years ending within two years after death; other trusts must pay estimated tax. Extending the two-year relief to all trusts is the trap.

questions.q: Which of the following must file a federal fiduciary income tax return (Form 1041) for the year?
choices: An estate with $500 of gross income and no taxable income
A complex trust with $400 of gross income and no taxable income
A simple trust whose only income is $550 of tax-exempt municipal bond interest
An estate with $650 of gross income
questions.exp: Under §6012, an estate must file if it has gross income of $600 or more; a trust must file if it has any taxable income or gross income of $600 or more. Tax-exempt interest is not gross income, so the municipal bond trust has no filing requirement.

questions.q: Under its governing instrument, a complex trust paid $25,000 of its current-year gross income to a qualified charity. The trust's gross income was $100,000. What charitable deduction may the trust claim?
choices: $10,000, limited to 10% of taxable income
$25,000, but only as an itemized deduction passed through to the beneficiaries
$0, because trusts cannot deduct charitable contributions
questions.exp: Section 642 allows an estate or complex trust an unlimited deduction for amounts of gross income paid to charity under the governing instrument. The percentage limits for individuals and corporations do not apply.

questions.q: In its final year, an estate had deductions exceeding its gross income and had an unused capital loss carryover. What happens to these items when the estate terminates?
choices: They are lost, because they belong to the estate
They pass through to the beneficiaries succeeding to the estate's property
They are deducted on the decedent's final individual return
They may be carried back three years by the estate
questions.exp: Under §642, unused loss carryovers and excess deductions in the termination year are allowed to the beneficiaries who succeed to the property. Without this rule they would expire with the entity.

questions.q: An estate has DNI of $50,000. During the year, the executor distributed a painting worth $80,000 to the decedent's niece under a specific bequest in the will, and $20,000 of cash to the residuary beneficiary. How much DNI is carried out to the niece?
questions.exp: A specific bequest of property or a sum of money paid in three or fewer installments is excluded from the distribution rules under §663, so it carries out no DNI. The residuary beneficiary is taxed on $20,000.

questions.q: A complex trust with DNI of $40,000 distributed stock to a beneficiary in satisfaction of a discretionary distribution. The stock had a basis of $10,000 and a fair market value of $25,000. The trustee did not make a §643 election to recognize gain. What is the amount of the distribution and the beneficiary's basis in the stock?
choices: Distribution of $25,000; basis of $25,000
Distribution of $10,000; basis of $10,000
Distribution of $25,000; basis of $10,000
Distribution of $25,000; the trust recognizes $15,000 of gain and the beneficiary's basis is $25,000
questions.exp: Without the election, an in-kind distribution counts at the lesser of basis or FMV ($10,000), and the beneficiary takes the trust's $10,000 basis. Gain recognition and an FMV basis occur only if the trustee elects.

questions.q: An executor paid $40,000 of estate administration expenses. Which statement about deducting these expenses is correct?
choices: They may be deducted on either the estate tax return or the estate's income tax return, or split between them, but the same amount cannot be deducted on both
They are deductible only on the estate tax return
They may be deducted on both the estate tax return and the estate's income tax return
They are deductible only on the decedent's final individual return
questions.exp: Section 642 prohibits a double deduction: amounts claimed on Form 1041 require a waiver of the estate tax deduction. The executor chooses whichever return produces the greater benefit.

questions.q: Within one year after the decedent's death, the estate paid $15,000 of medical expenses the decedent incurred during his final illness. Where may these expenses be deducted?
choices: Only on the estate's fiduciary income tax return
On the decedent's final individual return (subject to the AGI floor), if a waiver is filed, or on the estate tax return
On both the decedent's final individual return and the estate tax return
Only on the estate tax return
questions.exp: Under §213, medical expenses paid by the estate within one year of death may be treated as paid by the decedent when incurred, if the estate tax deduction is waived; otherwise they are deductible as a debt on Form 706. They are never deductible on Form 1041, and not on both returns.

questions.q: A simple trust earned $12,000 of qualified dividends and $8,000 of taxable interest and distributed all $20,000 of its accounting income to its sole beneficiary. How does the beneficiary report the income?
choices: $20,000 of ordinary income, because trust distributions lose their character
$20,000 of qualified dividends
$20,000 of other income not subject to tax because the trust paid tax
$12,000 of qualified dividends and $8,000 of interest income
questions.exp: Under the conduit principle of §§652 and 662, amounts distributed retain the character they had in the trust's hands. Treating distributions as a single ordinary income item ignores this rule.

questions.q: A trust's instrument requires it to distribute all income currently. This year, in addition to all income, the trustee distributed part of the corpus. How is the trust treated for the year?
choices: As a simple trust with a $300 exemption
As an estate with a $600 exemption
As a complex trust with a $100 exemption
As a grantor trust
questions.exp: A trust that distributes corpus during the year is a complex trust for that year (Reg. §1.651-1), even if it must distribute all income. The $100 exemption then applies because the trust does not qualify as a simple trust that year.

questions.q: A complex trust has DNI of $15,000, all from taxable interest. It distributed $25,000, including $10,000 of corpus, to its sole beneficiary. How much must the beneficiary include in gross income?
questions.exp: DNI caps both the trust's distribution deduction and the beneficiary's inclusion (§662), so the beneficiary includes $15,000; the excess is a tax-free distribution of corpus. Including the full distribution overstates income.

questions.q: A complex trust had $30,000 of taxable interest and a $10,000 capital gain allocated to corpus. It paid a $2,000 trustee fee charged to corpus and made a $15,000 discretionary distribution to its beneficiary. What is the trust's taxable income?
questions.exp: DNI is $28,000 ($30,000 − $2,000), so the distribution deduction is $15,000; taxable income = $30,000 + $10,000 − $2,000 − $15,000 − $100 exemption = $22,900. Omitting the corpus capital gain, which is taxed to the trust, gives $12,900.

questions.q: Which of the following is excluded from the distributable net income of a complex trust?
choices: Taxable dividends
Capital gains allocated to corpus and not distributed
Trustee fees charged to corpus (as a reduction)
Tax-exempt interest, net of allocable expenses
questions.exp: Under §643, capital gains allocated to corpus and not paid or set aside for beneficiaries are excluded from DNI. Tax-exempt interest is included in DNI (although excluded from the distribution deduction), and corpus-charged fees still reduce DNI.

questions.q: Which of the following may be deducted on an estate's fiduciary income tax return (Form 1041)?
choices: The decedent's personal living expenses before death
Executor's fees that are not claimed as a deduction on the estate tax return
The federal estate tax paid by the estate
The decedent's funeral expenses
questions.exp: Administration expenses such as executor's fees are deductible on Form 1041 if the estate tax deduction is waived (§642). Funeral expenses are deductible only on Form 706, and the estate tax itself is not deductible on Form 1041 (other than through the §691 deduction for income in respect of a decedent).

questions.q: A complex trust earned $30,000 of taxable interest and $10,000 of tax-exempt interest. It paid a $4,000 trustee fee that is not directly attributable to either type of income. How much of the fee is deductible by the trust?
questions.exp: Expenses allocable to tax-exempt income are nondeductible under §265; the fee is allocated proportionately, so 30/40 × $4,000 = $3,000 is deductible. Deducting the whole fee ignores the allocation to exempt income.

questions.q: A complex trust that is not in its final year has a net capital loss of $8,000 and no capital gains. How is the loss treated?
choices: The loss reduces DNI by $8,000
The loss passes through to the beneficiaries in proportion to distributions
The trust deducts $3,000 and carries the remaining $5,000 forward
The trust deducts the full $8,000 against ordinary income
questions.exp: A trust is subject to the same $3,000 net capital loss limit and carryover rules as individuals (§1211), and losses pass to beneficiaries only in the termination year. Capital losses generally do not enter DNI.

questions.q: An estate uses a fiscal year ending January 31, Year 2. During that fiscal year, the estate made income distributions to a calendar-year beneficiary in March through December of Year 1 and in January of Year 2. In which year does the beneficiary report the distributions?
choices: Year 1, for all of the distributions
Year 1 for the Year 1 distributions and Year 2 for the January distribution
Year 2, for all of the distributions
The year in which the estate files its return
questions.exp: Under §662, a beneficiary includes amounts for the estate's tax year ending with or within the beneficiary's tax year; the fiscal year ending January 31, Year 2 falls within calendar Year 2. This is the deferral benefit of an estate fiscal year.

questions.q: Which statement about the federal income tax rates applicable to trusts and estates is correct?
choices: They are taxed at the beneficiaries' marginal rates on all income
They are taxed at a flat corporate rate
They use the same brackets as single individuals
Their compressed brackets reach the highest marginal rate at a much lower level of taxable income than for individuals
questions.exp: Under §1(e), fiduciary rate brackets are highly compressed, which is a key reason trustees often distribute income to beneficiaries in lower brackets. Beneficiaries are taxed at their own rates only on distributed DNI.

questions.q: A single trust holds assets for two siblings, with each sibling's share administered independently and distributions from one share never affecting the other. In one year, all distributions were made from the first sibling's share. How is DNI allocated?
choices: Entirely to the sibling who received distributions, up to total trust DNI
To the trust, because no beneficiary received a required distribution
Separately for each share, as if each share were a separate trust
Equally between the two siblings, regardless of distributions
questions.exp: Under the separate share rule of §663, substantially separate and independent shares are treated as separate trusts for DNI purposes. This prevents one beneficiary from being taxed on income that belongs to the other's share.

questions.q: During its first year an estate earned $20,000 of interest and $10,000 of net rental income, paid $3,000 of executor fees that it elected to deduct on Form 1041, and distributed $12,000 to the residuary heir. What is the estate's taxable income?
questions.exp: DNI is $27,000, the distribution deduction is $12,000, and an estate's exemption is $600: $30,000 − $3,000 − $12,000 − $600 = $14,400 (§642). Using the $100 complex-trust exemption gives $14,900.

questions.q: A simple trust earned $20,000 of taxable interest in Year 1, all of which was required to be distributed currently. Because of an administrative delay, the trustee did not distribute the income until March of Year 2. When is the beneficiary taxed on this income?
choices: In Year 2, when the income is distributed
Never, because the trust pays the tax
In Year 1, because income required to be distributed is taxed to the beneficiary whether or not distributed
In Year 1 only if the trustee elects the 65-day rule
questions.exp: Under §652, a beneficiary of a simple trust includes income required to be distributed currently, whether or not it is actually distributed. The 65-day election applies only to complex trusts and estates.
